document.abstract: With about 1,600 vendors exhibiting at the NAB 2013 show, it's easy to see the direction and momentum of our industry. Or is it? Some product categories are traditional and define NAB at its heart: antennas, lighting, microphones, cameras, compression, tripods, speakers, displays, control surfaces, and so on. These are not considered information technology (IT) in nature, and this view will likely remain even if they sport an Ethernet connector. However, product categories such as signal and file management, transport, image processing, audio-visual (AV) editorial, review and approval, automation, scheduling, storage and archiving, element management, synchronizing methods, and distribution have taken on a distinctly IT nature in the past several years.

authors.bio: Al Kovalick has worked in the field of hybrid AV/IT systems for the past 20 years. Previously, he was a digital systems designer and technical strategist for Hewlett Packard. Following HP, from 1999 to 2004, he was the chief technical officer at Pinnacle Systems. For the next six years, he was a Corporate Fellow at Avid. In 2011, Kovalick founded Media Systems Consulting. — Kovalick is an active speaker, educator, author, and participant with industry bodies including SMPTE and the Advanced Media Workflow Association. He has presented more than 50 papers at industry conferences worldwide and holds 18 U.S. and foreign patents. He is the author of the book Video Systems in an IT Environment, 2nd edition. In 2009, Kovalick was awarded the David Sarnoff Medal from SMPTE. He has a BSEE degree from San Jose State University and MSEE degree from the University of California at Berkeley. He is a SMPTE fellow. Kovalick also writes the Cloudspotter's Journal for TV Technology magazine.
